title: Block close: the hidden light (Chagigah 12a)
hook: the light of creation was hidden away for the righteous

segments.voice: Yesterday, mystic kindness: the rebbe of Nemirov in peasant clothes, lighting a sick widow's stove before dawn. If not higher. Did you do your kindness quietly? Day one thousand two hundred ten.

"And God said, Let there be light: and there was light." That's the first day of creation. Keep reading Genesis and you reach the fourth day, when God makes the sun, the moon and the stars. So a careful reader stops and asks: if the sun came on day four, what was the light of day one? The rabbis of the Talmud asked exactly that. Their answer closes this whole block on Kabbalah and Hasidic thought, because it's a story about light that's still here, just out of sight.
screen: `LET THERE BE LIGHT.` → `THE SUN ON DAY FOUR.` → `WHAT WAS THE FIRST LIGHT?`

segments.voice: The hidden light. Turn it four ways. First, the passage. In the Talmud, tractate Chagigah, the sages teach that the light of the first day was a different light. By it, the first human being could see from one end of the world to the other. But when God foresaw generations who would misuse it, God hid it away, set aside for the righteous in the time to come. Second, a verse that keeps it close. The Psalm says: "Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart." Sown, like a seed. Hidden, but planted, waiting to come up. Third, where the light went. Teachings handed down in the Baal Shem Tov's name say the hidden light was tucked into the Torah itself, so whoever studies it with love can catch a glimmer now. That's the whole block in one picture. Look back over it. We began with the received, and a warning to enter carefully. Letters create. Without end, and ten lights. Love and limits, harmony, presence dwells. Look beneath the garment. Make room, broken things hold light, repair a shard. Then the Hasidim: no place without him, cling, joy opens, less me, two souls, you can repair, truth, fiercely. Hidden will. Named for towns, clothes remember, a ladder of song, women of the court, Hasidism beyond the court. Two paths inward, and mystic kindness. Fourth, the thread running through them. Again and again, these teachings say the light didn't leave. It's hidden, scattered, sown, waiting in a page, a song, a stove before dawn. Next comes a new block: the movements of modern Jewish life, side by side, without ranking.
screen: `THE LIGHT OF THE FIRST DAY.` · `LIGHT IS SOWN FOR THE RIGHTEOUS.` · `TUCKED INTO THE TORAH.` · `THE LIGHT DIDN'T LEAVE.` · then, large: `THE HIDDEN LIGHT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look for hidden light today, starting now. Settle, and close your eyes, or lower them. Breathe slowly. Think back across the last few weeks and find one moment when something good showed up where you didn't expect it: a kind word, a song, a person who stayed. Let it brighten in your mind for a few breaths. Then open your eyes and look around wherever you are. Rest your gaze on one ordinary thing, a cup, a window, a hand, and let it be enough just to look. The bell holds the time.
Block close. The hidden light of Chagigah: the light of the first day, put away for the righteous, which Hasidic teachers find sown in the Torah and in ordinary life. Today's word.
Your line: the hidden light. Today, when something ordinary catches the light, a face, a window, a page, stop for one breath and let it count. Day one thousand two hundred ten.

howItsDone: Jews read the creation story aloud in synagogue when the Torah reading cycle begins again, and the Talmud's teaching on the hidden light is studied in Chagigah and retold in kabbalistic and Hasidic teaching.

fork.setup: God foresees generations who would misuse the light of the first day. what does God do with it, says the Talmud?
options: hides it away for the righteous.
fork.reveal: the sages say God set it aside for the righteous in the time to come. Hasidic teaching adds that it was tucked into the Torah.

original.note: Hebrew: the hidden light, the light of creation stored away.

trapdoor: what you thought: a poetic way of saying things will get better.
what it means: the light of the first day, hidden for the righteous, still sown in the Torah and in ordinary life.
what a scholar hears: Chagigah 12a reading Genesis 1 against Job 38:15 and Psalm 97:11, and the Baal Shem Tov's light hidden in the Torah.

notes: Chagigah 12a paraphrased: the light of the first day, by which Adam could see from one end of the world to the other; God, seeing the generations of the flood and the dispersion, hid it for the righteous in the future. The Talmud's prooftexts (Job 38:15, Genesis 1:4, Isaiah 30:26 in some versions) are not quoted; please confirm.
The connection of Psalm 97:11 to the hidden light is a common association in later teaching rather than a line from Chagigah 12a itself; please confirm.
The teaching that the hidden light was placed in the Torah is given as 'handed down in the Baal Shem Tov's name' (cf. Degel Machaneh Ephraim, Bereshit); please confirm.
Block look-back lists the carries of days 1171–1209, abridged; please confirm this list reads well aloud.
Editor: softened 'every one of those teachings says the light didn't leave' to 'again and again', since several days (the courts, the clothes) don't say it; added day 1207's carry to the look-back.
